launches.title: Rindler - Turn Any Website Into An API For AI Agents
launches.tagline: Reliable web actions for AI agents, without integrations or scripts
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Rindler turns websites into deterministic APIs for AI agents. We map a site once into screens, actions, and structured outputs, so agents can read data and take actions quickly and reliably.

**Ask:** If you’re building an agent that needs to browse the web, compare products, fill forms, search listings, use authenticated portals, or act on third-party websites without an API, we’d love to help.

<https://youtu.be/V_nCIxYD-so>

## Problem

More products are starting to depend on AI agents that can do real work on the web: shop across retailers, pull housing listings, use job boards, submit forms, monitor prices, update back-office systems, and operate inside customer portals.

But most browser agents still treat every website visit like a new puzzle. On every run, they need to decipher the page, infer what matters, decide what to click, and recover when the page behaves differently.

That works for demos, but it breaks down in production. Real websites have pop-ups, login gates, cookie banners, bot defenses, slow-loading forms, dynamic filters, fragile dropdowns, layout changes, and pages that look similar but behave differently.

The result is slow execution, high token cost, and workflows that are hard to trust.

## Solution

Rindler maps websites into deterministic APIs for agents.

Instead of forcing an agent to re-explore a site every time, Rindler captures the site as structured screens, available actions, and typed outputs. Agents can then call actions like **search,** **add_to_cart**, or **download_records,** depending on the mapped site.

At runtime, Rindler handles the browser work through a remote MCP endpoint:

* Returning structured data
* Applying dynamic filters
* Managing popups, bot defenses, and layout changes
* Supporting authenticated flows

## Background

We started Rindler because “AI agent uses a browser” is compelling, but the current browser-agent loop is too brittle for teams building real products.

If an agent needs to use the same third-party site hundreds or thousands of times, it should not have to rediscover that site from scratch on every run.

Rindler is still a work in progress. Some sites map cleanly, others require more in-depth mappings, and bot-defended or logged-in sites may need a one-time credential or cookie capture.

We’re looking for feedback from founders building products where reliable web actions are part of the core workflow.

If there’s a website you wish your agent could use reliably, send it to us!

Companies buy an ERP expecting it to become the most powerful software in their stack. It runs finance, inventory, procurement, operations, reporting, and the workflows the business depends on.

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized gives developers a dedicated devbox in the cloud that still feels local. Your files stay synced to a real folder, ports show up on [localhost](http://localhost), and coding agents keep running when you close your laptop.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/JmaxNhEdLdc>

**The problem**

Coding agents can work for hours now. But only if you keep your laptop open.

You start a refactor, a migration, or a big build. Then you need to leave. Close the lid and the agent dies with it.

You can move everything to a VM, but now you're doing remote dev. Your files live somewhere else. Your ports need forwarding. Your terminal disappears when the connection drops.

Remote development still feels remote.

it shouldn't…

**The solution**

With Prized, one command puts your project on a dedicated devbox without giving up local development:

* **Real files on your Mac.** Prized syncs both ways into a normal folder, so everything keeps working the way it already does.


* [**Localhost**](http://Localhost)** stays [localhost](http://localhost)**. Servers running on the box appear on your Mac automatically, including loopback-only services and hot reload.


* **Sessions stay alive.** SSH lands in a persistent terminal session on the box, so disconnecting or closing your laptop doesn't stop the work.


* **Compute grows with the task.** Resize the box without rebuilding your environment or moving your project again.


* **Secrets stay out of the agent's hands.** For brokered secrets, the agent only sees a placeholder.

**The team**

We worked together at Gander (F24) building fleet management software for private jets. After the company's acquisition by Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), Marinos continued school at Stanford, and Hudson went on to be an engineer at Suno.

We built Prized for ourselves after getting tired of having to keep our laptops cracked open all the time. A raw VM kept the process alive but gave up the local workflow we actually wanted.

Check Prized out at [https://prized.dev](https://prized.dev/), or reach out at [founders@prized.dev](mailto:founders@prized.dev).

launches.tagline: The fastest way for non-engineers to ship secure internal tools.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized lets anyone at your company build and ship secure internal tools with AI. Company data comes pre-connected and scoped to what each person should see, every access is audited, and finished tools deploy behind your company's sign-in.

**Launch video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WILimoqemD4>

**The problem**

Building software has never been easier. And the people who need internal tools most, in ops, support, and finance, are done waiting on engineering.

So they build it themselves. They rip Claude Code or Cursor, pull straight from company data, and ship a working tool in an afternoon. No permissions. No audit trail. No one watching where the data goes.

Security is assumed to be fine because the tool is "just internal."

it's not…

**The solution**

People aren't going to stop building with AI. So we built them a place where it's safe.

With Prized, anyone can spin up a sandbox that comes with company data already attached, scoped to what they should see, with an audit trail on every access. 

From there it's whatever building style they like: describe the tool in our app builder and watch it take shape, or bring a coding agent like Claude Code and build it themselves. Shipping is one click, and the finished tool sits behind your company's sign-in.

The person who runs the workflow finally gets to build the tool for it. Safely, this time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/e426b427-8a79-4ca5-b462-b26b98db43e0)

**Secure by default**

Security is enforced in the infrastructure, not left to the person building the tool:

* **Least privilege per tool.** Every tool gets its own database role and integration scopes; it can read and write only what it was granted.
* **Credentials stay out of reach.** Secrets live in a broker and never touch the tool's code or the agent's context, so they can't leak or cross workspace boundaries.
* **Outbound traffic proxy.** External calls only go to explicitly allowed hosts, and integrations are read-only until someone turns writes on.
* **Admin visibility.** IT sees every tool in the org: who built it, what data it reads or writes, who can use it, and risky changes (like a destructive migration) need explicit approval before they ship.

**Your agent, our sandbox**

Already have a favorite coding agent? Bring it. It plugs into the same governed sandbox and ships the same way.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/fcfa68c5-8c9f-4d13-b37c-d526e733539a)

**The team**

We worked together at Gander (F24) building fleet management software for private jets. After the company's acquisition by Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), Marinos continued school at Stanford, and Hudson went on to be an engineer at Suno.

**Our ask**

If any of these describe you, we'd love to talk:

* You work in ops, support, finance, or RevOps and keep waiting on engineering for small tools.

Hey everyone, we're Mathieu, Thomas and Nicolas, two brothers and a best friend building COACH.

**TL;DR:** We're building the best coach for in-person sales ever built: reps record every in-person meeting from our app, and our AI turns it into precise, personalized coaching. <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yJB7wC3ddTM>

## The Problem

85% of sales in the world happen face-to-face. And in-person selling is brutally hard: a rep alone in someone's living room, reading signals, handling doubts, feeling the exact moment to push.

The best reps catch what no playbook can teach. That's why 20% of them bring in 80% of the revenue, and nobody knows what they're doing differently. The only way to find out is to physically be there: a ride-along, a full day, 100 km of driving to watch a single meeting. It doesn't scale.

## The Solution

COACH's AI learns how to close customers for your business, and closes the gap at every layer of the sales org:

* **Every rep gets a personal coach:** they record every in-person meeting from our mobile app, in-home, showroom, door-to-door, and walk out of each one with personal, precise feedback and a clear path to the next close. Our AI learns from your top 20% and coaches everyone to perform like them, starting each day with a morning brief on their weakest point. 90% improve on it in their first week.
* **The company gets a sales brain that learns how to close its customers:** every meeting feeds it. Why is one region closing twice as much as another? Which objection is killing deals this month? Leadership just asks, COACH has the answer.

Thousands of reps already run on COACH, live with the top 5 in-person sales companies in France, where we've lifted conversion rates by 32% on average, and dozens of reps 3–4×'d their numbers. We're now growing fast in the USA, where our first customers are switching from virtual ride-along platforms to COACH.

Every rep gets a coach. Your company gets a brain.

## The Team

At 18 and 21, we built Alsace Test: a 44-rep field sales team that did €3.5M in 14 months. Alsace made us fall in love with in-person sales, obsessed, actually.

And one thing was driving us crazy: same product, same material, same training, and one guy closed 4× more than the others. We were driving 2,000 km a week just to watch reps sell.

So we asked them to record themselves. Suddenly, without moving, we were listening to 10 hours of meetings a day. That was COACH before COACH.

In an AI-driven sales world, we're deeply convinced Zoom sales and call centers will soon be replaced by AI agents. Face-to-face selling will be the last human job on Earth. We're betting on it.

launches.tagline: Marble uses computer vision and voice AI to count inventory in minutes and a collection of AI agents that run inventory and labor management on autopilot.
launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re Arjun and Aakar, and we’re launching Marble (previously Truffle), the first AI-native operating system for the restaurant back-of-house.

**TL;DR:** We help restaurants control their two biggest costs, inventory and labor—saving them thousands of dollars per month in food waste, stockouts, and labor overage. We replace today's patchwork of disconnected point solutions, spreadsheets and clipboards with a single, easy to use system that actually does the work. We use computer vision and voice AI to count inventory 90% faster than manual counts, ML models to forecast item-level demand with 97% accuracy, and AI agents that run dozens of end-to-end workflows autonomously, including ordering, invoice reconciliation, scheduling, food prep, menu engineering, and more.

**The result**: We're live and scaling rapidly across multi-unit operations in the US and Canada. You can find us today in A&W Restaurants, The Kati Roll Company, Sophie’s Cuban, Kokomo NYC, HolyShred, Dead Letter No. 9 and many more. We’ve driven a 40% reduction in food waste, eliminated stockouts, and saved managers 30+ labor hours per week.

Check us out here:[ www.joinmarble.ai](http://www.joinmarble.ai)

**Our ask:** If you run or know someone who runs a restaurant, café, bar, or hospitality group, we'd love to talk. You can reach us at [founders@joinmarble.com](mailto:founders@joinmarble.com).

**Everyone knows someone who runs a restaurant, bar, or cafe - we’re also giving away $500 (or an Oura Ring) per referral!** [www.joinmarble.com/refer](http://www.joinmarble.com/refer) 

<https://youtu.be/Sbib-QYUH_Y> 

**The Problem**

Restaurant operators face an uphill battle. Ultra-competitive markets, rising food and labor costs, unforgiving hours, and after all of it, they take home 5% in net profit (if they're lucky).

A restaurant can be full all day and night, but it's the back office operations that determine whether that money hits the bottom line. Today that back office still runs on clipboards, spreadsheets, and guesswork. Inventory gets counted by hand, if at all, so no one has a real-time picture of what's actually on the shelf. Orders get placed from memory, so operators either over-buy (contributing to $150B+ in annual food waste) or under-buy and stock out on the exact items guests came for. Food prep and schedules are built on best-effort guesses, and invoices go unchecked while suppliers quietly raise prices line by line.

Every one of these is a margin decision, and every one is being made blind, leading to errors that compound every day, across every location.

**The Solution**

Marble runs the entire back office for restaurants. This centers around managing the two biggest cost centers (inventory and labor) and works in 4 phases:

* **Capture:** Computer vision + voice AI through our mobile app allow operators to count inventory 90% faster than manual counts, with 99% accuracy. No more hours spent counting items in a walk-in freezer with a clipboard (IYKYK). Invoices and deliveries are captured the same way.
* **Forecast:** ML models predict item-level demand for the weeks ahead at 97% accuracy. In addition to that, LLM-powered agents scan the signals a spreadsheet never sees - local events, weather, news, reservations, holidays - and adjust the forecast for what's actually happening around each location.
* **Act:** A set of AI agents run the workflows that actually move the needle on profitability: placing optimized orders, building demand-informed prep sheets, drafting schedules, proactively tracking and flagging waste, reconciling invoices, engineering menus, and more.
* **Learn:** This industry runs on tribal knowledge. We have built the product as a closed-loop system from day one: every count, correction, and order flows back into the platform as context that our agents carry forward, so Marble learns how each location actually runs, adapts to its patterns automatically, and gets sharper every day.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108273&key=user_uploads/1278164/1dd8a396-a754-4277-ad3b-1613bf1d4212)

**Team**

We’ve been close friends for nearly 10 years, since our freshman year at Michigan, and we're having a blast taking on this industry.

Aakar grew up managing the back office for his family's multi-unit quick service restaurants, where he saw the problem up close. He later covered the restaurant sector as an investment banker at Goldman Sachs before leaving to lead growth at an applied-AI startup in healthcare.

Arjun is a second-time founder and was previously a Senior Software Engineer at Bloomberg, where he led AI/ML initiatives on the Electronic Trading team. At Bloomberg, he built out complex trading systems that processed tens of millions of dollars daily.

launches.tagline: Record how you work and turn that into agents
launches.body:
screenpipe records what you do, see and hear on your computer, makes it searchable, and gives agents the context to understand how you actually work. The project has 20K+ GitHub stars.

<https://youtu.be/c1jV6E9pyug>

Most AI agents start every task with partial context.

They can read the prompt and apps you connect. They do not remember the meeting where a decision was made, the tab you opened last Tuesday, the exact steps you took to fix a problem, or the edge case you discovered while doing the work.

screenpipe runs quietly in the background and captures screen and audio context on your machine. Then you can ask:

* maintain a second brain for every person, projects, tasks, meetings


* turn the workday into a daily recap and time breakdown for standups or client billing
* maintain a personal CRM from the people, conversations, and follow-ups seen during the day
* find commitments mentioned in meetings or messages that never made it into a task list
* analyze repeated work and produce a list of workflows worth automating
* save prompts and context from Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT into a searchable journal

Agents can use screenpipe as long-term memory, so they work from what actually happened instead of only what you remembered to paste into a prompt.

The same foundation also works across team machines. Teams can map repeated workflows, generate SOPs, find bottlenecks, and identify automation opportunities across the tools where work actually happens.

screenpipe is open source and local-first. You control what gets recorded, can exclude apps, windows, and URLs, and choose where your data lives.

I’ve been building my own AI second brain since 2020, but it could only remember what I explicitly saved. I built screenpipe so my AI could understand what I was actually doing across my screen and conversations. Other people began using it for the same reason. Today, we’re turning that foundation into context for personal and team agents.

**Our ask**

Try screenpipe and comment with the agent you would build if it could remember everything you’ve worked on.

Try screenpipe: <https://screenpipe.com>

name: Definite
long_description:
Definite is where finance teams build everyday back-office agents on one live model of their books. We plug into your ERP, ledger, payroll, and payments read-only and compile everything into one clean model that stays current as money moves. Your back-office team then builds agents on top in plain English. We never write back and we never move money. The agents are yours, the plumbing is ours.

We met in first year computer science at Waterloo and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo. At Optiver they ran an n8n hackathon and the interns automated basically nothing. It couldn't talk to the systems that mattered. When we pitched banks and fintechs on agents, they kept telling us the same thing. The agent isn't the hard part, getting clean data out of their systems is.

Right now, automating anything in a back office means engineers hand-stitching data from a dozen sources in different formats on different schedules. Tools like n8n and Workato assume your data is already clean and joined. In finance it never is. So the teams with the most repetitive work and smallest budgets get nothing.

The hard part is the compiler. Every source gets cleaned, matched, and joined into one live model of transactions, invoices, vendors, and payments, and it has to stay right as money lands every day. 

Everyone throws engineers at this. We're doing it once so nobody has to again. Every back office is getting agents eventually. Whoever owns the data they read from owns the thing all of them depend on, and eventually the books themselves. That's what we're building.

launches.title: Definite - Turn weeks of regulatory reports into hours.
launches.tagline: The most accurate AI agents for financial reporting
launches.body:
_AI agents that run the entire regulatory reporting pipeline for banks, from raw ledger data to the filed report._

**_TL;DR_**_: Definite automates regulatory reporting for banks end to end, from raw ledger data to filed report, turning weeks of manual work into hours._ [usedefinite.com](http://usedefinite.com)

Hey! We're Gurshabd, Mazin and Farhan from Definite.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ji1ae8y_V4E>

**The Problem**

Proving to regulators that their books follow the rules is a constant, non-negotiable obligation for banks. Each report is thousands of numbers, personally signed off by an executive. Getting it wrong can mean a **fine up to a million dollars** over a single undetected error. Producing that proof is slow, and doesn't even guarantee it's correct. 

Here's where the current system breaks down:

1. **Wasted Hours:** A controller pulls data from the core system into Excel and maps it line by line by hand. By regulators' own estimate, one quarterly filing takes weeks of employee time, time pulled from higher-value finance work every quarter.
2. **False Confidence:** The software banks use to file checks formatting, not truth. A loan mapped to the wrong schedule line sails through every check. Nothing catches it until an examiner does, and by then it's not a mistake, it's a violation.

**The Solution**

**Report agents:** We connect to your books and our agents build the reports you owe.

**Verification engine:** Every number is recomputed from source records and checked against a versioned rulebook, so each line carries its rule and source data.

**Self-correcting agents:** When a check fails, the agent gets the reason and fixes it in seconds. Real exceptions come to your team with a drafted explanation, not a blank error. This loop is why our agents are the most accurate in finance.

**Receipts:** Every check produces a tamper-evident receipt you can hand an examiner or auditor.

Your team reviews and signs instead of building.

**How we got here**

Gurshabd worked at BitGo, a regulated crypto custodian, where attestations proving customer assets matched the ledger were built by hand every period. Farhan worked at Meta where he delved extensively into machine learning and building AI agents. Mazin saw Optiver recheck daily regulatory numbers by hand, then built LLM agents at [Boosted.ai](http://Boosted.ai) and learned finance people won't act on AI output unless every number comes with its source.

The lesson from all three: in finance, producing a number is cheap, proving it is the job. On two public reporting benchmarks, DeepSeek V3 with our verification engine outperformed GPT-5 on reconciliation accuracy (FinBalance) at roughly 50× lower cost, and beat the entire published field on XBRL calculation validation (FinAuditing).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105798&key=user_uploads/2947446/1b80714c-9a38-4d02-a037-ab05ad2c9205)

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR:** AI agents are quietly pulling secrets off your employees' laptops — and your security gateway can't see it. Traceforce installs in under 5 minutes and gives you a full inventory of every AI app, MCP, and skill running on every device, then lets you block the dangerous stuff in real time. Built by the ex-Clumio engineering team. Traceforce is already deployed on 3,000+ devices across six enterprise customers, with 40+ active pilots worth $3M+ in ARR. Try it free at [www.traceforce.ai](http://www.traceforce.ai).\
\
**The incident that started this**\
At our last company, an AI coding agent running on a developer's laptop scraped what looked like database credentials and pushed them straight into a public GitHub repo. It took us _weeks_ to investigate, rotate credentials, and clean up the fallout. We got lucky — they were dev-environment creds, so no customer was affected. Next time, nobody will be that lucky.\
\
That's the whole problem with AI at work now: ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and Claude Code are everywhere on employee devices, wired into your data through MCPs and skills that no one is tracking. The tools your security team already owns — gateways, proxies, enterprise APIs — never see any of it, because the risky action happens _on the device_, before it ever hits the network.\
\
**Why us**\
We're Xia and Varun. We ran engineering at Clumio, a cyber-resilience company acquired by Commvault in 2024, where Xia was Director of Engineering and Varun was tech lead. We've spent our careers building security infrastructure — and we validated this problem with 50+ CISOs and CIOs before writing a line of code. Every one of them said the same thing: \_I need to see and control this without slowing my engineers down.\_\
\
**Why on-device — and why gateways can't do this**\
Competitors sit at the gateway or plug into enterprise APIs. That misses the self-adopted AI tools employees install themselves, and it can't see how an agent is actually connected to your data via MCPs. Traceforce runs on the endpoint, so we see the full picture — which AI apps are running, what MCPs and skills they're wired to, what data they can reach — and we can _warn or block_ an unsafe action the moment it happens, not after it's already on the network.\
\
**What you get**

* Install in <5 min. Full inventory of every AI app, MCP, and skill across your devices within 30 minutes.
* Discover shadow AI and see exactly how each agent connects to your data sources.
* Real-time controls: warn and block unsafe actions (like uploading a client list to a chatbot) before they happen.
* Open-source MCP pentesting: we also built [mcp-xray](https://github.com/traceforce/mcp-xray) to dynamically detect vulnerable MCPs — try it today.

\
**Traction**

* Securing 3000+ employee devices across 6 medium-sized enterprises.
* Customer quote from a leading database provider with over 500 employees: “To govern AI, we need full visibility into AI usage before we can place any type of controls. Traceforce gives us both visibility and control we needed”.
* 40+ Active pilots including multiple Fortunate 500 enterprises.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a0OPq8vdDV0>\
\

Hey everyone! We’re David and Michael, co-founders of FlowManual.

**What FlowManual is**: AI preconstruction for General and MEP contractors, executing projects while cutting risk. 

**TL;DR:** Construction contractors waste hundreds of hours monthly on manual tasks, sifting through 500-page PDFs only to miss fine print that can cost tens of thousands. FlowManual automates the back-office work before and during construction, so teams can reliably secure and complete projects faster than ever before.

<https://youtu.be/aO5fBj_3kpU>\
\
**The Problem:**

Meet Jeremy. He’s a project manager at a mid-sized contractor, and his job is to secure projects and then make sure the company doesn’t lose money on already thin margins.

A bid invite lands in his inbox. To put together one number his firm can send in, Jeremy has to read thousands of pages. A 400-page project manual, drawings, insurance, spec sections, and so much more. Buried somewhere inside all this print is a line that can ultimately decide whether this job makes or loses money. From a liquidated-damages clause to a scope item sneakily handed to the mechanical contractor, if Jeremy misses it, it’s a $5K-$10K mistake.

Jeremy’s got one week, three other bids on his desk, and no way to read all of it as carefully as he’d like. So he reads what he can and sends in a number.

Say he wins. A change in the signed contract by the General Contractor or a sneaky difference in vendor pricing costs the company thousands after the fact. Every step of the way requires hundreds of pages of reading and referencing done under a deadline. And Jeremy does this for every job.

**The Solution:**\
FlowManual automates these historical workflows that contractors run on, allowing teams to submit bids and complete projects faster than ever before. Here’s a couple major features:

* AI Takeoffs from drawings
* Drawing comparisons / overlay
* Bid leveling
* Contract Review

Our software doesn’t do the job for you, but it works alongside you to reduce time spent and mistakes made.

**About Us:**\
Michael and David were college roommates and engineers at Harvard. When renovations for a heater in our dorm took 6 weeks, we poked at the problem, realizing it stems from a larger issue. Through hundreds of conversations with professionals, we found an industry that ran on file cabinets, Excel, and page-by-page manual review.\

##### We're building the most token-efficient coding agent in the world. The reason it works is GitNexus, our open-source knowledge graph for your codebase.

<https://youtu.be/-ErU4cCRSlQ>

##### The problem

Coding agents don't understand your repo. They grep, they guess, they re-read the same files, and they stuff half your codebase into a context window hoping the answer is in there somewhere. You pay for every one of those tokens, and the agent still misses the cross-file relationship that mattered.

The bottleneck isn't the model. It's context.

##### What we built:

GitNexus indexes your repository into a knowledge graph (symbols, call paths, imports, ownership, history) and serves the agent exactly the context a task needs, instead of everything it might need.

It's one connected stack:

* The knowledge graph. Run npx gitnexus analyze and you have it
* A coding agent that runs on top of it
* Automated PR review grounded in the same graph

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110659&key=user_uploads/1607382/1d3e51af-d3b5-4ee6-b0c3-b80bc4337c3e)

##### The proof:

On the DeepSWE benchmark, we ran the same agent with our graph and without it:

* 37% to 68.4% pass rate. Nearly twice the bugs solved
* Half the cost per fix, with fewer tokens
* On the hardest tasks, the gap more than triples

name: PokerClubHub
long_description:
TL;DR: PokerClubHub is the first licensed poker club platform. We protect players’ deposits and allow anyone to open their own poker club and make money.

Regulated online poker sites like PokerStars have open player pools and thus are full of pros and bots, driving players to unregulated private clubs.

Existing poker club platforms like ClubGG have no payments processing. Players deposit with a club owner by sending them crypto for play-money chips. In theory, these chips can be exchanged back for money. However, players can get scammed and withdrawing takes ages.

This model is also broken for honest club owners who have to manually process hundreds of deposits a day. They lose out on rake when they sleep and struggle to get players to trust them.

On PokerClubhub, players deposit with PokerClubHub, not the club owner. We handle all deposits and withdrawals for the club owner, saving them time and increasing their earnings. We pay the rake (if any) to club owners as affiliate fees.

We hold the same gaming license as BetHog (built by founders of FanDuel) and Nexa Poker (part of World Poker Tour). Player deposits are secured using Fireblocks.

long_description:
Executor.sh is an MCP gateway that allows you to sign in once to all of your integrations and use them with any client.

We enable you to connect your agents to anything (MCP, GraphQL, OpenAPI) so regardless of what you're trying to connect agents to you're able to.

launches.title: Executor — One place to connect your agents to everything
launches.tagline: Connect your tools once and every agent has them, with permissions you control
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Executor is your tool gateway. Connect every service and every account once, set per-tool permissions, and any MCP-compatible agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, whatever ships next) reaches all of it through one endpoint. Try it at [executor.sh](https://executor.sh).

https://youtu.be/NWYFpDW02Dw

## The problem

You don't have one agent anymore. You have Claude Code, a ChatGPT account, Cursor, maybe a box in the corner running jobs overnight. Three problems follow:

1. **Every agent wants its own OAuth into everything.** You connect your calendar to the tenth harness in a slightly different way, tokens expire, connectors deprecate, and each agent is missing something when you need it.
2. **Most connectors stop at one account per service.** One Google login means your agent sees your work calendar or your personal one, never both. Your flights land in one inbox, your meetings in the other, and no agent can reason over your actual day.
3. **Permissions are an afterthought.** Once an agent holds a token, it can do anything that token allows. Giving an agent your email shouldn't mean trusting it to never hit delete.

## What Executor does

Connect once in Executor, and sever all the one-off connections.

Each integration gets credentials plus a per-tool policy: **always allowed**, **needs approval**, or **blocked**. Point any MCP-compatible agent at Executor and it has everything.

- **All your accounts, not just one.** Accounts are connections: work and personal Gmail, two calendars, a staging and a production Stripe, side by side. Every agent sees all of them.
- **One tool shape.** MCP, OpenAPI, and GraphQL integrations all normalize into a consistent name + schema. 1,600+ tools collapse into a single ~1k-token surface instead of ~280k tokens of tool definitions.
- **Safe by default.** Executor preserves operation semantics (GET vs DELETE, destructive hints, GraphQL mutations), so agents auto-run safe operations and ask before risky ones.
- **Sandboxed execution.** Tool calls run in an isolated JavaScript sandbox; secrets are injected host-side, so the model never sees a raw token.
- **Team-ready.** Per-user and shared credentials. Onboard the team once, not per agent per person.

Because enforcement lives in Executor rather than in any agent framework, you can adopt whatever new agent ships next week without re-thinking data access. You keep everything first-party connectors offer and gain what they don't: multiple accounts per service, per-tool policies, and one place to see and revoke access.

## How to use it

- **Local:** open-source (MIT) desktop app and CLI, everything stays on your machine
- **Self-hosted:** a Dockerfile that lets your team own all its data
- **Executor Cloud:** hosted, nothing to manage

## Traction

- 2,800+ GitHub stars, ~14k npm downloads/week, ~3,000 users on the local version

## Background

Solo technical founder, previously at Vercel. Before Executor I built [answeroverflow.com](https://www.answeroverflow.com) and grew it to 1.5M monthly users as a solo dev, bootstrapped.

## Asks

1. **Try it and tell me where it breaks.** [executor.sh](https://executor.sh) has a "Copy prompt" setup you can paste into your agent to get started.
2. **Intros:** if your team (or one you know) is drowning in per-agent integration setup, I'd love an intro: rhys@executor.sh
3. **Star the repo:** [github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor](https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor)
4. **Want a walkthrough?** Grab a time: [cal.com/rhys-sullivan/executor-chat](https://cal.com/rhys-sullivan/executor-chat)

launches.tagline: AI that finds and fixes OS-level vulnerabilities across device fleets
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** For companies running large fleets of OS-level endpoints (running GPU clusters, having a network of cloud devices, or deploying on-device), Palisade detects and fixes operating-system vulnerabilities (privilege escalation, remote code execution, memory corruption) that are extremely hard to detect and mitigate without applying AI to kernel-level data (syscalls, eBPF traces, process/memory events, network packets). A fix that used to take weeks to roll out, Palisade now applies in minutes across every endpoint.

Hey YC! I'm Prince, an ML researcher and engineer who dropped out from Caltech at 18 to build Palisade.

**What’s the problem:** Modern attacks increasingly target the operating system, but most security products only observe the network, cloud, or application layers. That leaves OS vulnerabilities among the hardest problems to detect and the slowest to remediate across a fleet.

**Why I’m building this:** Since I was 16, I have done plenty of professional red-team and blue-team security work. One pattern kept showing up: OS-level vulnerabilities were consistently the hardest to handle. Detection required low-level visibility, and even after identifying a vulnerability, rolling out a mitigation across hundreds or thousands of machines often took weeks. My background in both machine learning and operating systems convinced me this didn't have to be a manual process, so I built Palisade to automatically detect and remediate these vulnerabilities at the kernel level across an entire fleet.

**What Palisade does:** Palisade watches your systems at the kernel level—syscalls, eBPF traces, process and memory events, and network packets—and uses AI to find OS vulnerabilities other tools miss, then implement the fix automatically across every endpoint.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106995&key=user_uploads/2688178/fa8c6d6a-b058-4f44-87d0-5511d038718b)

_The Palisade control plane, live against a real kernel (LSM-BPF). The live feed at the bottom: every row is a real syscall decision._

The vulnerabilities it catches are the ones you can't see from the app or network layer alone:

* Privilege escalation
* Remote code execution
* Memory corruption

Most are caught before an exploit ever happens, and the fix is applied immediately, fleet-wide. The same patch that used to take weeks now lands in minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106995&key=user_uploads/2688178/2f4e756d-1348-44a2-bdce-bb3491925da5)

_The host audit: real findings ranked by severity. The bottom one is the cloud-metadata exposure: the same path behind the Capital One breach. One click on **Apply fix** and it's installed as a kernel rule._

Palisade can already detect and fix real problems:

* CVE-2024-1086: use-after-free in the Linux kernel's netfilter (nf_tables); local privilege escalation to root
* CVE-2025-6019: libblockdev/udisks privilege escalation to full root
* CVE-2025-32463: sudo --chroot local privilege escalation to root

**Who it's for:** Companies running a lot of OS-level endpoints, where a single kernel vulnerability multiplies across the whole fleet. Whether it’s network servers or GPUs, we have you covered.

<https://youtu.be/CTVhq7jfTPY>

**Our asks:**

* Intros: if you run a large fleet of OS-level endpoints, or know a security/infra lead who does, I'd love an intro.
* See the demo and tell me if you’d use it. Brutal feedback welcome.

— [prince@palisade-ai.com](mailto:prince@palisade-ai.com), <https://calendly.com/prince-palisade-ai/30min>, DMs welcome

launches.title: Hyperprobe: On-call Agent for engineering teams
launches.tagline: The fastest way for coding agents to debug incidents live in production.
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR:** AI writes most of our code now. Debugging it when it breaks in production is still slow, because the value that explains the failure was never logged. HyperProbe is an on-call agent for engineering teams. It takes an open incident to a confirmed root cause by dropping read-only probes into your running service and capturing the exact variable state logs don't have. No redeploys, no restarting the app. \
\
📹 **Launch Video: [https://youtu.be/QtaZrQ8_Uk8](https://youtu.be/QtaZrQ8_Uk8)**

**🚧 The Problem**

Team ships faster than ever with agents that write most of our code. This is already shrinking the useful context engineers need to debug AI written code. Not helped by the limited telemetry added in the same code by AI. So when something breaks in prod, the first instinct for engineers is to open logs or throw them to agents. But if the line you are looking for is not there, agents will start guessing the root cause on limited data, forcing engineers to collect more logs by redeploys.

The result: our best engineers become our on-call team, incidents stay open longer, and patches come from data that never capture production context, so issues recur.

You can see where that leads. In September last year, a public fintech in India paid out $5 million after failed transactions were incorrectly marked successful. NYSE the same year miscalculated price bands for 40 symbols, printing trades so wrong they had to be reversed. Same pattern: the code ran clean, wrote the wrong state, and neither logs nor traces could show it.

 ✅ **What Hyperprobe does**

HyperProbe gives engineering teams an on-call agent that works the incident and takes it to a confirmed root cause, live in production.

* **Plan:** the agent picks up the alert from PagerDuty, Datadog, or Slack, then reads your logs and traces to locate the file and line. The easy incidents resolve right here.
* **Probe:** logs not enough? places read-only virtual breakpoints on the suspect lines and captures the exact variable state live, across services. No redeploys, no restarts. 
* **Confirm:** the diagnosis is verified against real captured evidence, not a guess. Your engineer gets a confirmed RCA and commits the fix.

There are two pieces. An SDK that runs inside your service, and an MCP server your coding agent talks to. The SDK is what makes setting probes (virtual breakpoints, log or metric) possible without a redeploy. 

### **🔍 A few examples**

* **An intermittent 500 that won't reproduce locally:** catch it live with full variable state 
* **A third-party API misbehaving:** see the exact payload and response
* **A function returns a wrong value with no error:** see what it computed and why
* **Anything that only happens in prod:** stop redeploying with console.logs

🚀 **The team**

We've both lived this problem. Shailendra ran production at scale. Karan was a senior architect at a SaaS company. Before this, both spent three years building production SDKs for a testing product, learning the hard parts of pulling real runtime state out of a running service without breaking it.

Every incident we watched came down to the same question: what was the actual value at the moment it broke. Nobody built it for the way engineers debug with coding agents now. So we did.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110401&key=user_uploads/3173209/ddf3d8d0-2bd4-4a8c-9547-fa5ea2496469)

### **🎁 Why now**

For thirty years the expensive part of software was writing it, and every tool got built for that. Generation is now nearly free, but the cost didn't disappear. It moved downstream, to figuring out why the generated code broke in production.

And that system is now mostly code no human wrote or holds in their head. When it breaks, the engineer has less context than ever, and their first move is already to hand it to the coding agent. That agent only has your logs and traces, so it guesses. We give it the evidence instead, captured live from the running code at the point of failure.

### **🙏 Our ask**

* If you're an engineer tired of the redeploy loop, debugging code you didn't write at 2 AM, try it on your own service.**,** first investigation in 10 min:[ https://docs.hyperprobe.co/quickstart](https://docs.hyperprobe.co/quickstart)
* If your best engineers have become your on-call team and you want that fixed, let us work one real incident from your stack, free: <https://calendly.com/shailendra-hyperprobe/30min>

name: Mirrors
long_description:
Mirrors provides regression testing for AI agents.

Teams shipping agents constantly change prompts, models, and tools, and there's no way to test any of it. Agents call bespoke internal tools and APIs no test framework can reproduce, so most teams ship on vibes.

Mirrors rebuilds the tools your agent calls from your own production traces, then replays real sessions against every change before it merges. You see which tool calls changed, which arguments moved, and where state landed differently. And when something fails, we tell you whether your agent regressed or something upstream moved.

Built for teams whose agents take irreversible actions. Refunds, record updates, outbound email.

Runs in your CI on every PR.
